title: Microsoft Copilot: Agent Mode in PowerPoint builds presentations from Work IQ
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licence entitlement and both governance controls are supported by Microsoft's text. It correctly distinguishes included Work IQ grounding from the separately billed Work IQ API, and leaves the feature's undocumented default state open.

claims.claim: Agent Mode in Copilot in PowerPoint can create presentations based on a user's Work IQ.
claims.quote: Now with Agent Mode in Copilot in PowerPoint, you can create presentations based on your Work IQ.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes saving users the effort of finding files, meetings and emails to compose relevant slides.
claims.quote: Build rich presentations without the heavy lift of finding all the right files, meetings, and emails to compose relevant slides.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot automatically gathers relevant files, meetings and emails to help build presentations.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint now uses Work IQ to automatically gather relevant files, meetings, and emails to help build presentations.

claims.claim: The release-note entry appears under July 01, 2026.
claims.quote:
## July 01, 2026
Updates released between June 17, 2026, and July 01, 2026.

claims.claim: The release notes list Windows for this entry.
claims.quote: Create presentations with Work IQ using Agent Mode in Copilot in PowerPoint [Windows]

claims.claim: The release notes direct users to open PowerPoint, select Edit with Copilot and choose a presentation based on Work IQ.
claims.quote:
Open PowerPoint and select 'Edit with Copilot'.
Choose to create a presentation based on your Work IQ.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The release notes tell users to review and customise the generated slides.
claims.quote: Review and customize the generated slides with the gathered content.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The integration accesses only authorised content.
claims.quote: This integration reduces manual effort and improves content relevance while maintaining data security by accessing only authorized content.

claims.claim: Work IQ is an intelligence layer enabling agents to access and reason over organisational data, content and tools.
claims.quote: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data, context, and tools.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview documentation says Copilot in Word, PowerPoint and Outlook support sensitivity label inheritance for newly created content.
claims.quote: Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook support sensitivity label inheritance for newly created content.

claims.claim: Content gathering replaces the previous manual search and compilation of presentation resources.
claims.quote: Previously, users manually searched for and compiled these resources.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Copilot works with Microsoft Graph content the user has permission to access.
claims.quote: Content in Microsoft Graph, such as emails, chats, and documents that you have permission to access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing user permissions remain the data-access boundary.
claims.quote: Semantic Index honors the user identity-based access boundary so that the grounding process only accesses content that the current user is authorized to access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The privacy page says full work data through Work IQ and semantic indexing is only available to users with the Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Access to full work data as part of Work IQ and semantic indexing is only available for users with the Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ grounding is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium).
claims.quote: Work IQ is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), whereas the Work IQ API is a distinct usage-based billing offering

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents for Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents. It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.claim: The distinct Work IQ API offering is usage-based for custom apps, agents and integrations.
claims.quote: the Work IQ API is a distinct usage-based billing offering that can be purchased and consumed independently for custom apps, agents, and integrations.

claims.claim: Work IQ API usage is billed through Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[0].note; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn names no separate licence specific to Agent Mode in PowerPoint with Work IQ as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent Mode PowerPoint Work IQ licensing price credits; read Copilot overview, Work IQ overview and release notes. Results describe Premium entitlement and separate API billing, not a feature-specific licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn names no separate price specific to Agent Mode in PowerPoint with Work IQ as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent Mode PowerPoint Work IQ licensing price credits; read Copilot overview, Work IQ overview, release notes and Plan licensing and cost excerpts. No separate price for this feature appeared.

claims.claim: Learn names no separate feature-specific meter for Agent Mode in PowerPoint with Work IQ as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent Mode PowerPoint Work IQ licensing price credits; read Copilot overview, Work IQ overview, release notes and Plan licensing and cost excerpts. The documented Copilot Credits meter concerns the distinct API offering.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated this feature's default state or what happens on arrival if a tenant does nothing.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent Mode PowerPoint Work IQ default enabled admin setting turn off; 555874 Work IQ PowerPoint default rollout. Read roadmap, release-note entry, Copilot overview and Work IQ API enablement; no feature-specific default stated.

claims.claim: No source states that this Work IQ presentation feature changes existing behaviour for users without the Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Searched: 555874 Work IQ PowerPoint default rollout; Agent Mode PowerPoint Work IQ licensing price credits. Read roadmap, release notes, Copilot overview and privacy pages; Basic capabilities are described, but no such change is stated.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote:
go to the Users > Active users page.
Select the row of the user
In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps.
Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PowerShell assigns a licence using Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @().
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: At least License Administrator or User Administrator is needed to assign licences.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote:
Open PowerShell as an administrator and run the following command:
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires the organisation to be licensed for Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires SharePoint Advanced Management to be available.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery controls discovery from selected SharePoint sites in Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including tenant-wide content discovery.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect experiences operating on content already in use, such as summarising an open document.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is described as a temporary governance control while permissions are reviewed.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is designed as a temporary governance control that gives organizations time to review and right-size access while continuing their Copilot deployment.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.where: Governance controls: Work IQ on/off; Open questions
claims.claim: The Copilot overview says Work IQ can be turned on or off.
claims.quote: You can turn Work IQ on or off.

claims.claim: With Work IQ off, Copilot responses are not grounded in Microsoft Graph and Work IQ.
claims.quote: When Work IQ is off, Copilot responses aren't grounded in Microsoft Graph and Work IQ.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot overview does not identify the location or owner of its stated Work IQ on/off setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ turn on off setting PowerPoint Agent Mode Microsoft Graph grounding. Read the full Copilot overview: it says 'You can turn Work IQ on or off' but gives no setting location or controlling role.

claims.claim: How the overview's Work IQ on/off setting relates to this PowerPoint feature remains undocumented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ turn on off setting PowerPoint Agent Mode Microsoft Graph grounding. Read Copilot overview, release notes and Work IQ API enablement; results cover Business Applications and custom agents, not this setting's effect on this feature.

claims.claim: The licence-assignment row is a general entitlement control, not a setting specific to Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: When you use the Active users page to assign or unassign licenses, you assign or unassign users licenses to products.

claims.claim: The Restricted Content Discovery row is a general site-discovery control, not a setting specific to Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.
